Function: Used to check the configuration after generation
Author: Nguyen Quan and Codex

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Timer control register. Defines software control or observable state for the timer.

Bits.Description:
Timer enable. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Set after programming period, prescaler and channel modes; clear before changing active configuration.

Values:
0x0 timer stopped;
0x1 shared counter and configured channels enabled.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Counter direction select. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Program while the timer is stopped; it selects the terminal count and reload direction.

Values:
0x0 count upward from zero through PERIOD;
0x1 count downward from PERIOD through zero.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.
None

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Timer period shadow register. Defines software control or observable state for the timer.

Bits.Description:
Counter period shadow value. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Writes while the timer is enabled update the shadow value and commit atomically with pending prescaler and compare/PWM shadows at the next update boundary. While disabled, the value is loaded before counting starts.

Values:
0x0 to 0xFFFFFFFF unsigned terminal count in timer ticks.

Unit: timer counter ticks.

Limits: the value is unsigned and shared by all implemented channels.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Timer period shadow register upper word. Read as zero and writes are ignored when PARA_COUNTER_WIDTH=32.

Bits.Description: Timer period shadow value. Holds bits[63:32] when PARA_COUNTER_WIDTH=64; ignored in the 32-bit profile.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: 16-bit timer prescaler shadow register. Divide factor is PSC + 1; values commit at update boundary while running.

Bits.Description: Prescaler divide value. Counter advances once every PSC+1 timer-core clocks; zero means divide by one. Values written while running commit atomically at an update boundary.
Reserved; reads zero and writes are ignored.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: DMA burst configuration and clear. Programs one to four logical records per capture or compare/update req/ack burst and clears the DMA handshake state after an error.

Bits.Description:
Capture DMA clear. Writing 1 starts recovery of the capture req/ack handshake after a DMA error or reset.

Usage: Write 1 to drop o_dma_cap_req, wait for any capture stream beat to finish, flush the capture FIFOs and queue, then return to idle. Software must not issue it while the DMA is mid-burst unless recovering from an error; write 1 while the clear is busy is ignored.

Values:
0x0 idle or clear finished;
0x1 clear requested; hardware writes 0 when the clear completes.

Unit: none.

Limits: the bit self-clears; a software write has priority over the hardware clear in the same cycle. Captured records still in the queue are discarded.

Compare/update DMA clear. Writing 1 starts recovery of the compare/update req/ack handshake after a DMA error or reset.

Usage: Write 1 to drop o_dma_cmp_req, wait for any compare/update stream beat to finish, discard the staged and batched records, then return to idle.

Values:
0x0 idle or clear finished;
0x1 clear requested; hardware writes 0 when the clear completes.

Unit: none.

Limits: the bit self-clears; a software write has priority over the hardware clear in the same cycle. Records already committed to the compare queue are kept.
None

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Timer channel 0 configuration register. Defines software control or observable state for the timer.

Bits.Description:
Consecutive sample threshold. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Program one less than the number of consecutive equal samples required to accept a new filtered input level.

Values:
0x0 require one equal sample;
0x1 to 0xF require two through sixteen consecutive equal samples, using the programmed value plus one.

Unit: consecutive equal samples.

Limits: software encoding is N minus one, from zero through fifteen.

Output polarity. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Select whether the compare/PWM waveform is driven with normal or inverted polarity. The force-value and idle-level fields specify physical pin levels.

Values:
0x0 normal, non-inverted waveform;
0x1 inverted waveform.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Output idle level. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Select the physical output level driven when this channel's output function is disabled.

Values:
0x0 drive low while disabled;
0x1 drive high while disabled.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Output force enable. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: When set, override compare/PWM/one-pulse waveform generation with the physical level selected by force_value.

Values:
0x0 normal channel waveform or idle behavior;
0x1 force the selected physical output level.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Forced physical output level. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Select the physical pin level used while force_en is set.

Values:
0x0 force output low;
0x1 force output high.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Capture timeout enable. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Enable no-edge timeout monitoring for this capture channel.

Values:
0x0 timeout disabled;
0x1 timeout enabled.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.

Capture timeout start selection. This field defines or reports its timer function and state.

Usage: Select whether timeout starts when the capture channel is enabled or after the first qualified edge.

Values:
0x0 start timeout at channel enable;
0x1 start timeout after first qualified edge.

Unit: none.

Limits: none.
Software re-arm control. Zero enables automatic re-arm after a pulse; one requires a software re-arm command while idle.
Software re-arm command. A low-to-high transition arms an idle one-pulse channel; software clears this bit before issuing another command.
None

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Live shared counter low word. A read event at this address latches the full counter snapshot in 64-bit mode.

Bits.Description: Low 32 bits of the shared counter; reading this register captures the matching 64-bit snapshot.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Coherent shared counter high-word snapshot.

Bits.Description: Bits[63:32] captured by the preceding low-word read; reads zero in the 32-bit profile. Reading high returns the snapshot and releases it.

Table - Register Definition.Descriprtion: Shared DMA queue occupancy and reservation levels.
